title: Director, Quality and Safety Capability Development
text:
**Location:**

Rosedale Office Building

**Department:**

Patient/Medication Safety

**Shift:**

First Shift (United States of America)

**Standard Weekly Hours:**

40

**Summary:**

 

**SCHEDULE:** Monday-Friday, 8a-5p

 

***This role will work onsite at our Rosedale office building in Fort Worth, TX.***

 

The Director, Quality and Safety Capability Development leads the strategy, design, and delivery of organization-wide quality and safety learning programs. This role builds sustainable improvement capability across the health system by equipping leaders, physicians, clinicians, and staff with the knowledge, skills, and tools needed to improve outcomes, strengthen safety culture, reduce variation, and advance continuous improvement. The Director partners across clinical, operational, and administrative functions to support organizational performance and transformation.

 

**Strategy & Leadership**

* Lead the strategic direction for quality and safety capability development across the organization.
* Align education and development initiatives with organizational quality, safety, and performance priorities.
* Partner with executive and physician leaders to identify improvement opportunities and support risk reduction efforts.

**Program Development**

* Design and implement scalable quality and safety learning programs for leaders, clinicians, physicians, and staff.
* Develop curricula focused on continuous improvement, patient safety, leadership effectiveness, and data-informed decision-making.
* Utilize blended learning approaches to increase engagement and application of learning.

**Capability Building**

* Strengthen organizational capability in quality improvement and patient safety methodologies.
* Support leaders and teams in applying improvement science to clinical and operational challenges.
* Promote consistent improvement frameworks, tools, and practices across the health system.

**Leadership Engagement**

* Collaborate with clinical and physician leaders to develop and deliver impactful education.
* Build leader capability to drive quality and safety performance within their areas of responsibility.

**Integration & Measurement**

* Coordinate learning initiatives across departments to create an aligned approach to quality and safety development.
Partner with analytics and operational leaders to measure program effectiveness and organizational impact. 

 

**JOB REQUIREMENTS:**

 

**Experience**

10 years of pediatric healthcare experience including experience in clinical practice, healthcare education, workforce development, professional training, quality improvement, or patient safety. 



**Education**

Master's degree from an accredited college or university in Education, Adult Education, Instructional Design, Health Education, Organizational Development, or a related field. 

 

**Licensure, Registration, and/or Certification**

* Lean Certification or Six Sigma Green Belt required.
Certified Professional in Patient Safety (CPPS) or Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality (CPHQ) required. 

 

**About Us:**

 

Cook Children’s is an equal opportunity employer. As such, Cook Children’s offers equal employment opportunities without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, physical or mental disability, pregnancy, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected class in accordance with applicable federal laws. These opportunities include terms, conditions and privileges of employment, including but not limited to hiring, job placement, training, compensation, discipline, advancement and termination.

 

Cook Children’s is a Texas-only employer. If you are hired, you will need to maintain your primary residence within the state of Texas, along with all licenses and credentials required for your position throughout your employment.
